title: American Cancer Society: Alkaline Diets, Baking Soda, and Cancer Cell Myths
content: There is no scientific basis to claim an alkaline diet or consuming sodium bicarbonate neutralizes or cures cancer in humans. Dietary changes cannot alter systemic blood pH. Human blood pH is strictly regulated by the kidneys and respiratory system within a narrow pH range of 7.35 to 7.45 regardless of food or beverage intake. Proponents of alternative alkaline therapies often claim that cancer cells cannot survive in an alkaline environment; while isolated cell cultures in petri dishes behave differently, in living human physiology stomach acid rapidly neutralizes ingested sodium bicarbonate and lemon juice. Delaying evidence-based oncology treatment in favor of unproven home remedies such as lemon and baking soda mixtures puts patients at severe life-threatening risk.
